hook: A scratched, slightly corroded green metal cabinet opens onto a maze of rusted corridors, and that is about all the setup you need. The pleasure is in the small physical details: flickering household bulbs, cold leaking pipes, water you can actually drink. Pay attention to what happens when the doors close, because everything else in the file hinges on it.
whyItMatters:
This is a straightforward bigger-on-the-inside object, and it shows how much dread a Safe classification can hide. The procedures amount to a lock and a guarded key, yet the description quietly lists starvation, a large predator and a growing count of lost D-class.

The document is also built around exploration: an agreed equipment pack and a numbered set of expeditions, one of them locked, invite you to imagine the trips into the dark.
thingsToNotice:
Closing the doors does two things at once: it cuts every form of contact and moves the entrance somewhere else in the maze, so anyone inside at that moment has no reliable way back. The corridors are exactly the cabinet's height and width, which makes the space feel like the locker stretched out forever.

The discovery scene is grim on reflection: the cabinet sat unlocked at the centre of an empty steel mill, surrounded by sleeping bags and bags of clothes left by homeless people who had been vanishing from the area. The cabinet itself dates to the early 1950s, but objects pulled out of it are much older, a detail the file states and then leaves alone.
